name: Turmeric
preparation: Churna (powder), Paste with warm water or milk
safety_notes: Generally safe. High doses may upset stomach or aggravate Pitta.
historical_note: Subject of landmark 1995 US Patent revocation by CSIR via prior art proof.

name: Ashwagandha
preparation: Churna with warm milk or ghee
safety_notes: Avoid during acute infection. High doses may cause GI distress.
historical_note: Studied extensively for active compound withanolides.

name: Holy Basil
preparation: Infusion, Fresh leaf juice, Swarasa
safety_notes: May lower blood sugar. Exercise caution if taking hypoglycemia medication.

name: Brahmi
preparation: Swarasa (fresh juice) or Medhya Rasayana
safety_notes: May cause mild stomach upset or nausea if taken on an empty stomach.
historical_note: Research highlights active bacosides for cognitive health.

name: Neem
preparation: Leaf paste, Decoction, Oil application
safety_notes: Not recommended during pregnancy or for small children. Bitter taste may induce mild nausea.

name: Ginger
preparation: Fresh juice (Ardraka), Dry powder (Shunthi)
safety_notes: Use cautiously in hyperacidity, ulcers, or active bleeding conditions.

name: Amla
preparation: Fresh fruit, Churna, Chyawanprash component
safety_notes: Very rich in vitamin C; excessive sourness may temporarily aggravate Pitta in sensitive individuals.

name: Triphala
preparation: Churna mixed with warm water at bedtime
safety_notes: Excessive doses may cause diarrhea or abdominal cramps.

name: Gotu Kola
preparation: Fresh juice, Dried leaf powder, Decoction
safety_notes: Extremely high doses over extended periods may affect liver function; monitor long-term use.

name: Shatavari
preparation: Root powder with warm milk and ghee
safety_notes: Caution for individuals with kidney conditions or severe fluid retention.

name: Guduchi
preparation: Guduchi Satva (extract powder), Swarasa, Kwath
safety_notes: May lower blood glucose levels; monitor closely if taking anti-diabetic medication.

name: Arjuna
preparation: Bark powder, Arjuna Ksheerapaka (decoction with milk)
safety_notes: Should be taken under supervision if combined with cardiac or antihypertensive medications.

name: Licorice
preparation: Root powder, Chew stick, Decoction
safety_notes: Avoid long-term overuse in individuals with high blood pressure due to potential fluid retention.

name: Cardamom
preparation: Crushed seeds in tea, Powder
safety_notes: Generally safe. Excessive consumption may irritate gallstones.

name: Haritaki
preparation: Churna with warm water or honey
safety_notes: Avoid during pregnancy, acute exhaustion, or severe dehydration.

name: Cinnamon
preparation: Bark powder, Infusion in tea
safety_notes: Use genuine Ceylon cinnamon; Cassia varieties contain coumarin which impacts liver health in excessive doses.

name: Trikatu
preparation: Combined equal powder mix taken with honey
safety_notes: Pitta aggravating. Avoid in hyperacidity, ulcers, or internal burning sensations.

name: Aloe Vera
preparation: Fresh inner leaf gel, Asava fermentation
safety_notes: Avoid latex/outer skin portion during pregnancy due to potential uterine stimulation.

name: Vidanga
preparation: Fruit powder with warm water or honey
safety_notes: Contraindicated during pregnancy; consult a practitioner for appropriate dosage.

name: Guggulu
preparation: Purified resin tablets or decoctions
safety_notes: Avoid during pregnancy or acute inflammatory conditions; requires proper traditional purification (Shodhana).

name: Bhringraj
preparation: Bhringraj Taila (oil), Swarasa, Churna
safety_notes: Cooling nature; may trigger cold symptoms in highly sensitive Vata/Kapha individuals when applied topically at night.

name: Shankhpushpi
preparation: Syrup, Decoction, Powder with warm milk
safety_notes: May enhance sedation if combined with anti-anxiety medications; use under supervision.

name: Long Pepper
preparation: Vardhamana Pippali Rasayana, Powder with honey
safety_notes: Pitta aggravating in long-term continuous use without proper traditional vehicle (anupana).

name: Punarnava
preparation: Root powder, Kwath (decoction), Arishta
safety_notes: Use cautiously in severe hypertension or cardiac failure without medical monitoring.

name: Kutki
preparation: Fine root powder with warm water or honey
safety_notes: Extremely bitter; high doses act as a purgative and can cause diarrhea.

name: Manjistha
preparation: Decoction, Powder, Oil application
safety_notes: May temporarily color urine reddish or orange; harmless but noteworthy.

name: Malabar Nut
preparation: Swarasa (leaf juice), Syrup, Decoction
safety_notes: Contains vasicine; contraindicated during pregnancy as it may cause uterine contractions.

name: Bael
preparation: Unripe fruit powder, Fruit pulp beverage
safety_notes: Ripe fruit can cause constipation if taken in high quantities over long periods.

name: Fenugreek
preparation: Soaked seeds, Powder, Sprouted seeds
safety_notes: Pitta aggravating in high amounts; monitor blood sugar if combined with diabetic drugs.

name: Cobras Saffron
preparation: Flower bud powder with honey or butter
safety_notes: Generally safe in recommended dosages; use under supervision during pregnancy.
